generator.params.note: Drawing values no character gives, the ones the Columbia lily was drawn with by hand before (lilies, 2026-10-18): one stem from the bulb leaning a little, a lily flowering from its third year (a seedling bulb takes three to five), its stem coming up from the bulb with its leaves near full size, the lowest sixth of the stem bare, the leaves longest a little below the middle of the leafy part, and the raceme's top tenth in bud.

appearance.note: FNA vol. 26 (2002), Lilium (genus account, efloras.org, read 2026-10-18): filaments usually pale green or nearly translucent; style usually pale green. The colours are our reading of the words. The flower has no disc at its centre, so the tepals start from a small base (centre 0.08 of the radius).

traits.perennation.note: FNA vol. 26 (2002), Lilium (genus account, efloras.org, read 2026-10-18): herbs, perennial, bulbose; the bulb's scales numerous, fleshy and starchy.

traits.petal_shape.note: FNA vol. 26 (2002), Lilium (genus account): sepals and petals more or less lanceolate and narrowed or rarely clawed.

traits.petal_apex.note: FNA vol. 26 (2002), Lilium (genus account): sepal apex usually acute; petal apex usually acute, often more widely than the sepal's.

traits.anther_attachment.note: FNA vol. 26 (2002), Lilium (genus account): anthers versatile, oblong, 0.3-2.6 cm.

traits.fruit_type.note: FNA vol. 26 (2002), Lilium (genus account): fruits capsular, 3-valved, dehiscence loculicidal.

traits.fruit_posture.note: FNA vol. 26 (2002), Lilium (genus account): fruits erect, green maturing to brown.

traits.leaf_colour.note: FNA vol. 26 (2002), Lilium (genus account): blade green and somewhat lighter abaxially, rarely paler. The colour is our reading of the word, the mid-green the Columbia lily was drawn in by hand before.

traits.bark_colour.note: FNA vol. 26 (2002), Lilium (genus account): stems erect, green, sometimes purple, rarely glaucous. The colour is our reading of the word.

rules.note: How the herb program draws a lily from its flora's characters, a choice of the model's (lilies, 2026-10-18): the flower from its tepals, each on its own stalk arching to the posture its flora gives (the flowering plants' flower_tilt), the stem's leaves in the whorls its flora counts, its raceme long enough to space its flowers on their stalks, and its leaves from the longest its flora measures down to the shortest, as the campanulids' herbs are drawn.

generator.params.flower_size.why: A lily's tepals reach from the flower's small base (0.08 of its radius) to the rim, so the flower drawn is twice a tepal's length across, before its tepals curve back.

generator.params.pedicel.why: A flower stands on a stalk as long as its flora measures the pedicel; where none is given, half again a tepal's length, about the shortest the North American floras give for their lilies.

generator.params.flowers.why: A stem bears as many flowers as its flora counts in the raceme, up to 60.

generator.params.raceme.why: A lily's flowers stand apart on their long stalks: each stalk's foot a little under half a stalk's length above the one below, so the raceme is as long as its flowers need, as a share of the stem.

generator.params.flower_angle.why: A lily's flower stalk leaves the stem at a slant, steeper where the flower faces up; it arches from there to the posture its flora gives.

generator.params.nodes.why: A lily with its leaves in whorls bears as many whorls as its flora counts, the few scattered leaves between them left out; one with scattered leaves bears one up its leafy part every fifth of a leaf's length, which crowds them as the floras' numerous leaves (Bailey's 50 to 100).

generator.params.stem_radius.why: A lily's stem is about 8 mm through at its foot for each metre of its height, as the Columbia lily was drawn by hand before.

generator.params.leaf_angle.why: A leaf stands from the stem as its flora's posture says: pressed up, rising at a slant, held out nearly level (the floras' horizontal and drooping at the tips), or hanging.

generator.params.leaf_length.why: A lily's longest leaf is as long as the longest its flora measures; the leaves below and above it are shorter, down to the shortest it measures.

generator.params.leaf_top.why: A lily's topmost leaf is as short, for the longest, as the shortest leaf its flora measures (the floras' leaves reduced distally).

generator.params.leaf_base.why: A lily's lowest leaf is as short, for the longest, as the shortest leaf its flora measures.

generator.params.bud_size.why: A bud is drawn half a tepal long, its size while it fattens to open, as the Columbia lily was drawn by hand before.
